title: Microsoft Purview: new custom permissions menu in the Information Protection File Labeler
summary: The briefing passes: Microsoft documents the client releases, authentication refresh and both File Explorer controls it describes. The Windows-only wording should be narrowed because the cited release notes also document a macOS client in preview.

claims.where: title; What's changing; Why it matters; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The roadmap plans to replace the existing File Labeler custom permissions UI with the familiar Office custom permissions menu.
claims.quote: This feature borrows the familiar custom permissions menu in Office and replaces the existing custom permissions UI in the Microsoft Purview Information Protection File Labeler.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: The new menu enables viewer, restricted editor, editor and owner permissions to be assigned to multiple groups simultaneously.
claims.quote: The new menu enables viewer, restricted editor, editor and owner permissions to be assigned to multiple groups at the same time.

claims.claim: File Labeler is a component of the Information Protection client.
claims.quote: It has the following components: ... Information protection file labeler

claims.where: What's changing; summary; Scope; rationale: impact
claims.claim: File Labeler applies sensitivity labels and encryption using File Explorer, making its custom permissions users the audience for the dialog change.
claims.quote: Information protection file labeler | Used to apply sensitivity labels and encryption using File Explorer.

claims.claim: The Information Protection client runs on Windows only.
claims.quote: This client runs on Windows only and replaces the Azure Information Protection (AIP) unified labeling client.
claims.fix: Replace the Windows-only wording in both sections with 'The Windows Information Protection client includes File Labeler; the client release notes also document a separate macOS client in preview.' The differing documentation is at https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/information-protection-client-relnotes, which states 'The Microsoft Purview Information Protection client for macOS is currently in preview and is offered as two separate applications: File Labeler and File Viewer.'

claims.quote: Searched: Purview File Labeler custom permissions Microsoft Graph supported group types external domains; supported groups security distribution groups dialog. Read client release notes and Graph groups-overview excerpt; no menu-specific group eligibility stated.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Open questions
claims.claim: The known-issues page says the File Labeler Address Book button does not open the Outlook address book when new Outlook is used.
claims.quote: If you use new Outlook, the Address Book button in the **Select _users, groups, or organizations" field in the Information Protection File Labeler app doesn't open the Outlook address book. You must add email addresses manually.

claims.claim: The menu is an option within a client covered by the product's existing sensitivity-labeling subscription requirement, supporting the included licensing model.
claims.quote: You must have a cloud-based subscription for sensitivity labeling using the Microsoft Purview Information Protection client or scanner.

claims.claim: No admin UI for controlling the File Labeler Protect with custom permissions option is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: EnableCustomPermissions portal UI; Purview Information Protection client turn off custom permissions admin UI label policy advanced settings. Read client advanced settings, Windows client customizations and create-sensitivity-labels excerpt; no admin UI found.

claims.where: controls[0].api; rendered table; Why it matters; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: Set-LabelPolicy -Identity "Global Policy" -AdvancedSettings @{EnableCustomPermissions="False"} hides the Protect with custom permissions option for users covered by the label policy.
claims.quote:
Set-LabelPolicy -Identity "Global Policy" -AdvancedSettings @{EnableCustomPermissions="False"}
This example configures the specified advanced setting for the sensitivity label policy name Global Policy.

claims.claim: No admin UI for hiding the Apply sensitivity label with Microsoft Purview File Explorer entry is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: LegacyDisable Purview UI hide File Explorer; new custom permissions dialog default enable disable UI LegacyDisable. Read Windows client supported customizations and client advanced settings; registry mechanism documented, no corresponding admin UI found.

claims.where: controls[1].api; controls[1].note; rendered table; Governance controls
claims.claim: Creating the DWORD value LegacyDisable with any data under HKEY_CLASSES_ROOT\AllFilesystemObjects\shell\Microsoft.Azip.RightClick hides the whole Apply sensitivity label with Microsoft Purview File Explorer entry.
claims.quote: To hide the Apply sensitivity label with Microsoft Purview right-click menu option in File Explorer, create the following DWORD registry key that has the value name of LegacyDisable and any value data: HKEY_CLASSES_ROOT\AllFilesystemObjects\shell\Microsoft.Azip.RightClick

claims.claim: When EnableCustomPermissions is turned off, users by default cannot see or change custom permissions already set on an encrypted document.
claims.quote: When you configure the advanced client setting EnableCustomPermissions to turn off custom permissions in File Explorer, by default, users are not able to see or change custom permissions that are already set in an encrypted document.

claims.claim: Setting EnableCustomPermissionsForCustomProtectedFiles to True lets users see and change an encrypted document's existing custom permissions in File Explorer when custom permissions are otherwise turned off.
claims.quote:
users can see and change custom permissions for an encrypted document when they use File Explorer and right-click the file.
Key: EnableCustomPermissionsForCustomProtectedFiles
Value: True

claims.claim: Set-LabelPolicy functions only in Security & Compliance PowerShell.
claims.quote: This cmdlet is functional only in Security & Compliance PowerShell.

claims.claim: Set-LabelPolicy requires assigned permissions.
claims.quote: To use this cmdlet in Security & Compliance PowerShell, you need to be assigned permissions.
